tasks.title: Self-locate the six census roots on import.meta.url, each with a root-mismatch guard
acceptance: THE SIX FILES, as named in every criterion below: src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts, src/renderer/src/beachcomber/Beachcomber.hygiene.test.ts, src/renderer/src/helm/no-paths.test.ts, src/renderer/src/pods/wording.test.ts, src/renderer/src/transcript/tool-summary.test.ts, src/renderer/src/state/isolation.test.ts (base 5e5e7d4 roots at :94, :43, :49, :50, :43, :37 respectively). No code in any of the six calls process.cwd(): `grep -nE 'process[.]cwd[(]'` over the six paths in the worktree returns no line, or only lines that are inside comments (each such hit listed in the report and shown to be prose).

Each of the six derives its scan root from its OWN import.meta.url using the repo idiom fileURLToPath(new URL(<relative>, import.meta.url)) — the Gate 1 decision (discussion.md:34-38; models tests/router/helpers.ts:27 and tests/unit/pod-manager/marker-single-definition.test.ts:47-49) — with fileURLToPath reached through a dynamic import whose specifier is NOT a string literal, because tsconfig.web.json sets "types": [] and the renderer rule at hygiene.test.ts:302-313 (base) flags any literal 'node:' specifier that importSpecifiers (:198-211) can read. The same idiom, spelled the same way, in all six files.

Each root keeps the shape its consumers rely on: forward slashes only and no trailing slash (hygiene.test.ts:184-186 slices ROOT.length + 1; isolation.test.ts:84 slices RENDERER_ROOT.length + 1). isolation.test.ts's RENDERER_ROOT, which today has no backslash normalisation (:37), is normalised the same way as the other five.

Each of the six files contains a test that compares the path of the file itself, derived from its own import.meta.url, against the path that file's scan root implies for it (ROOT joined with the file's repo-relative path; for isolation.test.ts, RENDERER_ROOT joined with state/isolation.test.ts), and fails with a message containing the words `root mismatch`. NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER, a fact about this geometry: the session worktree is nested inside the main checkout (C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene), so a prefix/startsWith comparison against a cwd-derived root HOLDS in the mismatched geometry and cannot go red; the next criterion would fail such a guard.

RED STEP, mismatched geometry (test discipline, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'): with the six guards added and the roots STILL derived from process.cwd(), run from cwd = C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate (the main checkout) `C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/node_modules/.bin/vitest run --root C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts src/renderer/src/beachcomber/Beachcomber.hygiene.test.ts src/renderer/src/helm/no-paths.test.ts src/renderer/src/pods/wording.test.ts src/renderer/src/transcript/tool-summary.test.ts src/renderer/src/state/isolation.test.ts`; the report shows the six guard tests failing, one per file, each failure message containing `root mismatch`.

RED STEP control, correct geometry: in the same pre-conversion state, `npm --prefix C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene test -- <the six repo-relative paths>` (cwd = the worktree for the script) passes all six guard tests — so the red in the previous criterion is caused by the geometry and not by a normalisation artefact such as slash direction or drive-letter case.
GREEN, mismatched geometry, after conversion: the exact mismatched-geometry command named in the RED STEP criterion reports all six files passed and zero failed tests, the six guards included.

PRESERVED (deliberately satisfied at startRef, stated so): after conversion, the mismatched-geometry run and the correct-geometry run report the same per-file test counts for the six files. Agreement alone cannot discriminate in this session (both trees hold identical content, orchestrator probe 2026-10-29); the green guards in the previous criterion are what show the mismatched run read the worktree's tree.

src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts still begins with its `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock (base :1) and is among the files the RED and GREEN runs above executed, so the idiom is proven under jsdom and not only under the node environment of the other five.

The six files' `declare const process: { cwd(): string };` declarations (base: hygiene.test.ts:76, Beachcomber.hygiene.test.ts:25, no-paths.test.ts:31, wording.test.ts:32, tool-summary.test.ts:25, isolation.test.ts:21) are removed, being dead once no file calls cwd: `grep -n 'declare const process'` over the six paths returns nothing.

`npm --prefix C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene run typecheck` exits 0 (both typecheck:node and typecheck:web) — vitest does not typecheck, and the six are compiled under tsconfig.web.json.

`npm --prefix C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene test` passes: 141 test files, and a test count equal to the base 2252 (orchestrator probe 2026-10-29) plus the tests this task added, with no existing test removed, skipped or weakened.

tasks.title: Reintroduction guard and four precision fixes in hygiene.test.ts
acceptance: Line numbers below are at base 5e5e7d4 and shift after T1; each site is also identified by its quoted text. REINTRODUCTION GUARD: hygiene.test.ts carries a test that walks every *.test.ts and *.test.tsx file under src/renderer/src, reads each with comments stripped (as the file's other code rules do, stripComments at :188-191), and fails listing every file whose code calls process.cwd(); on the tree at T2's end it passes.

The reintroduction guard is non-vacuous over the real tree: it asserts that its scanned population contains each of the six files T1 converted, by repo-relative path — hygiene.test.ts itself included, so the guard's own needle is shown not to trip it (every needle in this file is assembled from fragments, :69-71).
Positive control: the reintroduction predicate flags a synthetic sample containing a process.cwd() call, asserted in the file.

Near-miss: the reintroduction predicate does NOT flag a synthetic `declare const process: { cwd(): string };` sample — the declaration shape all six files carried at base and that __tests__/harness.tsx:88 still carries (with on/off members) — asserted in the file.

DEMONSTRATED DISCRIMINATION (test discipline, Coverage): with a process.cwd() call injected into the CODE of hygiene.test.ts at one named line, `npm --prefix C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/census-root-hygiene test -- src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts` fails the reintroduction guard naming src/renderer/src/__tests__/hygiene.test.ts; the injection is reverted and the report names the line.

BORDER_PROPERTIES docblock and constant agree (base :622-638; the docblock reads 'Every property that declares a border WIDTH, including the shorthands.' while the constant omits border-block, border-inline and their four longhands, which CENSUS_BORDER_PROPERTIES at :1506-1520 lists). Direction pinned at Gate 2: the docblock is NARROWED. It no longer claims the shorthands in general; it names the physical properties the constant lists, names border-block, border-inline and their longhands as deliberately absent, and says they are held repo-wide by CENSUS_BORDER_PROPERTIES. The constant's members are unchanged, and the CENSUS_BORDER_PROPERTIES docblock 'WIDER THAN `BORDER_PROPERTIES` ABOVE' (:1468) and the borderOffenders(...border-block...) toEqual([]) assertions at :1680 and :1864 still hold unmodified.

PRESERVED (satisfied at startRef by the presence-only check, labelled at Gate 2; meaningful only together with the next two criteria). RETIRED-ID SELF-CHECK, shipped shape: the exemption self-check (base :1129-1140, today presence-only via text.includes) accepts a code occurrence of the retired literal that is the argument of an absence assertion, in the shape the exempt file ships (lanes/LaneRail.test.tsx:180, `expect(screen.queryAllByTestId('lane-row-pin')).toHaveLength(0);`, its only code occurrence), and the real exempt file still passes it.

RETIRED-ID SELF-CHECK, presence use: the self-check's predicate rejects a synthetic exempt-file sample whose only occurrence of the retired literal is a presence query (e.g. a getByTestId call), asserted in the file. At base this sample passes the presence-only check.

RETIRED-ID SELF-CHECK, every occurrence: the predicate rejects a synthetic sample carrying one absence-assertion occurrence AND one presence-query occurrence of the retired literal — the check holds for every code occurrence, not for some — asserted in the file.

RETIRED-ID SELF-CHECK, stale exemption (preserved): an exempt file carrying no retired literal in code still fails the self-check, as the base check's 'is exempted but carries no retired literal in CODE' message does at :1138.

Prose count, base :850 ('Beachcomber has two, Helm one, the shell four.'): the shell count reads five.
